chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Musa al-Hamdani, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Aban ibn Ghailban, who said:

I found thirty dinars one day, so I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about that. He said to me, 'Where did you find it?' I said to him, 'I was returning to my house when I found it.' He said, 'Return to the place where you found it and make it known. If its claimant comes after three days, give it to him; otherwise, give it in charity.'
ai.seo_question: What is the procedure for handling found money in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the specific procedure for handling found money (luqata), emphasizing the finder's duty to return to the exact spot and announce the find to verify ownership. The three-day waiting period serves as a practical window for the owner to recognize the item, after which the finder may retain it or distribute it as charity, reflecting the Shia emphasis on both justice and social welfare in property rights.
